grades.question: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?

expected.answer: Yes; resolve Growth actions in chosen order, so the first placement can extend the second. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining Presence from either chosen track. Use only the highest uncovered Energy number and highest uncovered Card Plays number, not their sum.

requested_parts: May second Add Presence use first as range origin?
Which track disks may be taken?
observed.answer: Yes. Resolve multiple Add Presence placements sequentially, so the first new disk may be the origin for the second. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track. For normal income and plays, use the highest uncovered number on each track separately; do not add uncovered values together.

evidence.text: - **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

**Gain Energy:** Take Energy equal to the **highest uncovered number** on your Energy/Turn track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own **highest uncovered value**; neither track adds its uncovered numbers together. Unspent Energy carries over between turns; it is individual and cannot ordinarily be transferred to another Spirit.

grades.question: In a Ravage a land has one Town, one Explorer and two undamaged Dahan, with no Defend or prior Blight. Resolve damage to land, Dahan, surviving counterattack and resulting Fear if the players destroy the Town.

expected.answer: Invaders do 3 Damage simultaneously to land and Dahan, adding one Blight, killing one Dahan and damaging the other by 1. The surviving Dahan still deals 2 Damage, destroying the Town and generating 1 Fear. Dahan do not absorb/prevent land damage; partial Dahan damage clears at Time Passes.

observed.answer: The Town and Explorer deal 3 total Damage: the land takes 3 and receives one Blight; the Dahan take 3, killing one and leaving the other with 1 marked Damage. The surviving Dahan then deals 2 Damage, enough to destroy the Town (2 Health), generating 1 Fear.

evidence.text: Example: A Town, Explorer and two Dahan with no Defend cause 3 land Damage (one Blight), and simultaneously 3 Dahan Damage (one dead, one damaged). The survivor can destroy the Town for 1 Fear. [CORE pp.9,11]

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. [FAQ number-of-counterattacks-when-dahan-counterattack-early; .bu6oc8y]

Fear effects are not Spirit Powers. For “each player,” one player follows all instructions, then the next; choices can affect anywhere allowed by the card without the player's own Presence or Power Range. Generic Presence/Sacred Site requirements can use any Spirit's; wording explicitly counting each Spirit's own sites is individual. The same piece can be chosen or moved by multiple players unless the card requires different choices. Fear effects last for the turn unless they change the board. For outcome timing, a card containing **only “each” instructions** creates one action per “each” (e.g., per player). A card mixing a global instruction with “each” instructions is one overall action with nested actions per “each”; complete that whole action tree before checking outcomes. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.

The original land still receives its Blight; cascading does not replace it. If a pool empties during this process, immediately follow the card's instructions, flip/refill as directed and continue unfinished Blight additions/cascades. Add the reverse side's printed number per Spirit from the box; **do not add the initial +1 again**. If an instruction must add more Blight **simultaneously** than remains on Healthy, flip immediately before that addition, carry the remaining old Blight into the newly created pool and fully resolve any immediate flip effects as nested actions, then return to add the required Blight. Do not add the setup +1 again. [FAQ .9v5kfqt]

Removing island Blight returns it to whichever side of the card is currently face-up (or the board pool if no card). A Blighted card never becomes Healthy again, however much Blight is removed. Removing Blight does not restore destroyed Presence.

grades.question: Explain how Elements apply to multiple thresholds and multiple Powers. May an innate be used twice with twice the Elements, may its levels use different lands, and how does an “Instead” level work?

expected.answer: Elements are checked, not spent, so may meet any number of Powers/thresholds. An innate is normally one use, regardless of surplus Elements. Use all met levels top to bottom on one target, with Instead replacing previous effects. May pretend to have fewer Elements for the entire Power, not cherry-pick levels.

requested_parts: How are Elements used across multiple thresholds?
How are Elements used across multiple Powers?
Can innate be used twice with twice Elements?
observed.answer: Elements are checked, not spent; the same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds. Having twice the Elements does not permit a second innate use, its levels use one target, and “Instead” replaces earlier effects.

evidence.text: An Innate is available each turn when its Element requirements are met; ordinarily it costs no Energy and uses no Card Play. Elements are **checked, never spent**. The same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds. Gain a card's Elements as soon as it is played, whether or not its text is used, and lose them as soon as it leaves play.

- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.

- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.

grades.question: A legal target lacks pieces needed for one printed instruction. May the Power still be used? May the player choose individual unwanted instructions to skip, or forego the whole Power and recover its Energy?

expected.answer: May use it; perform instructions in order, skipping impossible parts and doing the rest. Cannot skip possible mandatory instructions at will (apart from permitted choices, up-to, or selecting fewer Elements consistently). May forego the whole Power; no Energy refund, and played-card Elements remain while in play.

observed.answer: Yes, use the Power and do as much as possible. Possible mandatory instructions cannot be arbitrarily skipped (though “up to” permits zero). You may forego the Power but receive no refund.

evidence.text: - Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.

Use Fast Power Cards in play and eligible Fast Innates. Players choose their order; finish one Power before starting another. A Power cannot interrupt another Power. You may forego a Power entirely, retaining a played card's Elements but receiving no Energy refund. A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow: use it now or forego it.

grades.question: Explain gaining a new Minor or Major Power, including how many are drawn, where kept/unkept cards go, Major Forgetting options and the consequences of Forgetting a card already in play.

expected.answer: Choose Minor or Major, draw 4 from that deck, reshuffling its discard if needed; keep one in hand, discard the other three to its deck discard. Gaining a Major requires Forgetting any one owned card (hand, personal discard, in play, even new Major); forgotten Minor/Major goes to its deck discard, Unique under panel. Forgetting in-play immediately loses Elements and unused use; previously resolved effects persist for their normal duration.

observed.answer: Draw four from selected deck (reshuffling discard if needed), keep one in hand, and discard three to its shared discard. After a Major, Forget a card from hand, personal discard, or play, including that Major. Forgotten Minor/Major cards go to shared discard; Unique goes under the panel. Forgetting from play removes Elements and unused activation immediately, while resolved effect persists.

evidence.text: To **Gain a Power Card**, choose the Minor or Major deck, draw 4 (reshuffling that deck's discard if needed), keep 1 in hand, and discard the rest to that deck's shared discard. No hand-size limit applies and players may show their hands.

After **gaining a Major**, Forget one of your cards permanently. You may Forget from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under its Spirit panel, unavailable to ordinary Reclaim or gain. If you Forget from play, immediately lose its Elements and any unused activation; an already resolved effect persists normally. Each Major gained requires its own Forget; a single card cannot satisfy separate Forget requirements.

grades.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?

expected.answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated. An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of its Damage or Health. Remove likewise takes the specified piece off the board without requiring Damage to reach Health. Replace removes the original and puts the specified replacement in its place.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. grades.question: If a Town is replaced by an Explorer while retaining 1 Damage, does the replacement itself cause Fear, does the Explorer survive, and why? Can reduced Health destroy a piece without new Damage?

expected.answer: Replacement itself causes no Fear. Retained 1 Damage meets Explorer Health 1, so it is destroyed, giving no Fear for an Explorer. More generally, a piece is destroyed immediately once existing Damage meets its reduced/new Health, even without new Damage.

observed.answer: Replacement itself causes no Fear. The Explorer retains 1 Damage, which equals its Health 1, so it is immediately destroyed; it generates no Fear. Reduced Health can destroy a previously damaged piece without new Damage.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

grades.question: Can Blight cascade into an Ocean on a board with Ocean’s Presence? Can normal Growth Add Presence to that Ocean as if a Coastal Wetland, can it measure from existing Presence there, and how can Ocean put Presence Inland in the base game?

expected.answer: Cascade into that Ocean is legal. Normal Growth cannot treat it as Coastal Wetland to add there, but may measure from existing Presence in Ocean. Indomitable Claim explicitly ignores land-type restrictions and can place Ocean Presence Inland; ordinary adding Powers do not bypass its restriction.

observed.answer: Blight may cascade into Ocean on a board with Ocean’s Presence. Normal Growth cannot Add Presence to Ocean just because it counts as Coastal Wetland, but Growth Range may be measured from existing Ocean Presence. Ocean’s explicit group adding two Presence in any Ocean places only in Oceans; to put Presence Inland requires a specific exception such as Indomitable Claim.

evidence.text: - **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). grades.question: When Ocean Drowns a Town and a City, when is Fear earned and where do pieces go? In two-Spirit play how much Energy value is a drowned City worth, can change be made, and do Dahan yield Energy?

expected.answer: Fear earned immediately on destruction: 1 for Town and 2 for City. Drowned Invaders go on Ocean panel for later trade. Trade X printed Health for 1 Energy, X=Spirits, so in two-Spirit game City gives 1 Energy plus 1 Health change. Ignore Health modifiers; Dahan drown with no Energy benefit.

observed.answer: Drowning destroys Town/City, generating Fear immediately; drowned Invaders go on Ocean’s panel. In a two-Spirit game, a City’s printed Health 3 can be exchanged as 2 Health per 1 Energy, yielding 1 Energy with 1 Health of value left as change. Dahan yield no Energy.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. This post-action-tree correction uses the cleanup procedure below. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]

grades.question: Bringer uses a 2-Damage Power and then a separate 1-Damage Power on an undamaged City. What happens? What if 2 then 1 Damage are instructions within a single Power, and may a Repeat pretend-destroy the same piece again?

expected.answer: Separate Powers do not combine hypothetical Damage and each does nothing to undamaged City. Single Power’s instructions combine to would-destroy City and earn 5 Fear, leaving City actually unchanged. Repeat is separate action and can pretend-destroy same piece again if its own Damage suffices; cannot combine its hypothetical Damage with original.

observed.answer: Bringer’s separate 2-Damage and 1-Damage Power uses cannot combine hypothetical Damage; the undamaged City is not destroyed by either, so no Fear from that City. Within one Power, instructions can combine for the hypothetical destruction. A Repeat can pretend-destroy the same Invader again for Fear.

evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. This special rule does not Push Cities. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. evidence.text: - **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. grades.question: For a Range arrow within a Power’s effect text, where is the origin for a land-targeting Power? Where is it for a Spirit-targeting Power used by Spirit A that instructs Spirit B to act? Which Spirit’s Range bonuses apply, and if that internal arrow is Range 1 with A having +2 and B having no bonus, what Range can it reach from whose Presence? How does Blazing Renewal’s explicit measurement origin differ?

expected.answer: For a land-targeting Power, measure the internal arrow from the target land unless otherwise specified. For a Spirit-targeting Power, normally measure from the Presence of the Spirit following the instruction, B here, unless the text says otherwise. Apply the bonuses of the Power user A, not B: the stated Range 1 becomes Range 3 from B’s Presence. Blazing Renewal explicitly measures from the Power user A’s Presence, even when B adds Presence; its explicit origin overrides the default.

observed.answer: A land-targeting arrow starts at the target land. A Spirit-targeting arrow starts at the instructed Spirit B’s Presence. Apply A’s bonus: Range 1 +2 = Range 3 from B’s Presence. Blazing Renewal explicitly measures from using Spirit A’s Presence.

evidence.text: - **Internal Range origins:** A Range arrow inside a land-targeting Power's effects is measured from the **target land**, unless stated otherwise. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. grades.question: What is the required order of an individual Spirit's Growth, normal track Energy gain, and actual playing/paying for Power Cards? May the Spirit take its normal Energy income before finishing Growth or actually play/pay before Growth? If Growth uncovers a higher Energy number, is that number used for normal income in this same Spirit Phase?

expected.answer: The Spirit must complete Growth, then gain normal Energy, then play and pay for Power Cards. It may not take the normal income or actually play/pay cards before Growth. The normal income step follows Growth and uses the highest number then uncovered, including a higher number just revealed by that Growth, so the benefit applies in this same Spirit Phase. Players may plan their choices earlier; planning is not the formal play/pay step.

observed.answer: Each Spirit completes Growth, then normal track Energy gain, then card play/payment. It cannot take normal income or play/pay before finishing its Growth. If Growth uncovers a higher Energy number, use that highest uncovered number for income this same Spirit Phase.

evidence.text: Each turn follows **Spirit Phase → Fast Power Phase → Invader Phase → Slow Power Phase → Time Passes**. Finish a phase before beginning the next. Players choose the order of Powers within the appropriate Power Phase, completing one before the next. All players act simultaneously within a phase and may discuss freely. Each Spirit must finish its own Growth → Gain Energy → Play/Pay in that order, but may wait to see another Spirit's Growth or draws before making choices. **Every Spirit must finish the entire Spirit Phase before any Fast Power resolves.**

**Gain Energy:** Take Energy equal to the **highest uncovered number** on your Energy/Turn track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own **highest uncovered value**; neither track adds its uncovered numbers together. Unspent Energy carries over between turns; it is individual and cannot ordinarily be transferred to another Spirit.

grades.question: A Spirit still has Presence disks on its Presence tracks. When resolving an ordinary Add Presence instruction, may it choose to reposition one of its Presence already on the island instead of taking a track disk, or is repositioning permitted only after its tracks are empty?

expected.answer: It may reposition an existing island Presence instead of taking a track disk even while track disks remain. Empty tracks are not a prerequisite. Choose a normally legal destination using existing Presence, then take an own island disk; this does not uncover a new track benefit.

requested_parts: reposition while tracks still have disks
observed.answer: Yes. Add Presence may reposition any island Presence even with track disks remaining; it is still an Add Presence instruction.

evidence.text: - **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

grades.question: Wrap in Wings of Sunlight meets its threshold. Its target land initially has no Dahan, but Dahan are available in adjacent lands. Does its threshold’s “First, Gather up to 3 Dahan” happen before the base Move, so those Dahan can then be moved and the destination Defended, or must the base Move finish first because it is printed higher? Likewise, with Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship’s threshold, does its Invader-on-Invader Damage happen before or after Pushing the Explorers?

expected.answer: Wrap’s explicit First instruction Gathers before the base Move, allowing those gathered Dahan to be moved by the base effect and Defend 5 in the destination if at least one moves. Dissolve’s explicit Before Pushing instruction resolves its threshold Damage before the Explorer Push (after the preceding replacements). Such timing words override the default top-to-bottom position; they do not create another Power use.
source_refs: threshold First instruction and base Move/Defend

observed.answer: Wrap’s “First, Gather” threshold occurs before the base Move, allowing gathered Dahan to move and provide destination Defend. Dissolve’s Invader-on-Invader Damage resolves simultaneously before the Explorer Push.

evidence.text: - **Location-dependent effects:** **Wrap in Wings of Sunlight** resolves its threshold’s **First, Gather up to 3 Dahan** before its base Move; those gathered Dahan may then move and allow the destination’s Defend. It grants no Defend if zero Dahan move: there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their original land can count as Move if the Power permits. **Blazing Renewal** permits its target Spirit to add its destroyed Presence directly to one legal island land, not to tracks. Its printed “adds 2” is mandatory to the extent possible, using the Power user's Presence for its internal Range; it cannot deal threshold Damage with no destroyed Presence restored: “that land” refers to where it adds Presence. **The Trees and Stones Speak of War** deals 1 Damage per Dahan and grants Defend 2 per Dahan in its target land. Its threshold moves Defend 2 with each Dahan it Pushes, leaving the remaining Defend in the target. Each destination receives Defend 2 for each Dahan this Power Pushes into it. Only this Power's Defend 2 per pushed Dahan travels; separate Defend from another effect, such as Words of Warning, stays in its original land. A later Power moving those Dahan does not carry that Defend. [Core: .9v5kfqd, .9v5kfr0, .bu6oc8n, .bu6ocxq]

- **Core Power specifics:** **Song of Sanctity** is Slow, despite missing cost-circle ink in some printings. Its Explorer condition selects its effect: with Explorers, Push all of them; otherwise remove 1 Blight. This is not a free choice to remove Blight while Explorers remain. **Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship** line 3 Pushes all Explorers **to as many different lands as possible**, using every available legal destination up to the number of Explorers; its Invaders damaging each other do so simultaneously, **before** the Explorer Push as the threshold specifies. **Poisoned Land**'s threshold counts the Blight that its own earlier instruction added. **Tsunami**'s threshold adds Fear for each other Coastal land it affects. [Core: .7w4g9dg, .9v5kc31, .7w4ganc, .7w4g8q3, .7w4g8pc]

grades.question: For two Spirits, how are the Fear pool/deck and Invader deck prepared, what initial Blight pool is used with and without a Blight Card, and what final Invader action completes setup?

expected.answer: Use 8 Fear markers, 9 shuffled Fear cards divided 3/3/3 by Terror II and III dividers; Invader deck is 3 Stage I above 4 Stage II above 5 Stage III, randomized within each stage with one unused card per stage removed unseen. Initial Blight is 5 with a Healthy Island card (2 per player +1), or 11 without (5 per player +1). Setup Explore the top card normally and leave it face-up in Build; Ravage is initially empty.

requested_parts: Prepare the two-Spirit Fear pool and Fear deck.
State setup Blight with and without a card.
State the final Invader action of setup.
observed.answer: For two Spirits, put 8 Fear markers in the pool and use 9 shuffled Fear Cards in three groups of three, with Terror II and III dividers between groups. Shuffle each Invader stage separately, remove one unseen card from each, then stack 3 Stage I, 4 Stage II, and 5 Stage III cards. With a Blight Card, start with 2 per Spirit plus 1 total (5); without one, use the introductory pool of 5 per Spirit plus 1 total (11). The final setup action is reveal the top Invader card, Explore normally, then place it face-up in Build; Ravage starts empty.

evidence.text:
## Setup

**Deck preparation includes randomization, not just selecting counts:** shuffle all Fear Cards before taking the nine used cards; shuffle each Invader stage separately before removing its unseen unused card and stacking the stages.

1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.

2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.

3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.

4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.

5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.

6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.

7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

**Introductory alternatives (CORE p.3):** Choose a low-complexity Spirit: Lightning's Swift Strike, Vital Strength of the Earth, River Surges in Sunlight, or Shadows Flicker Like Flame. A new player may use its Power Progression: remove the listed Minor and Major cards from the shared decks and reserve them; on gaining a Power, take the next one into hand instead of drawing four. Gaining a Major still requires Forgetting a card. If everyone is new, omit the Blight Card and use the printed board pool: **5 Blight per Spirit +1 total** at setup, losing if it empties; there is no flip or ongoing Blighted effect. Do not use an Adversary or Scenario. Progressions are a teaching aid, not compulsory for low-complexity Spirits.

grades.question: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?

expected.answer: Yes; resolve Growth actions in chosen order, so the first placement can extend the second. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining Presence from either chosen track. Use only the highest uncovered Energy number and highest uncovered Card Plays number, not their sum.

requested_parts: Whether the second Add Presence may use the first placement as its range origin.
Whether uncovered Energy and Card Plays numbers combine.
observed.answer: Yes. Resolve multiple Add Presence placements sequentially, so a newly placed disk can be the next placement’s range origin. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own highest uncovered number; their numbers are not added together.

evidence.text: - **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

Fear effects are not Spirit Powers. For “each player,” one player follows all instructions, then the next; choices can affect anywhere allowed by the card without the player's own Presence or Power Range. Generic Presence/Sacred Site requirements can use any Spirit's; wording explicitly counting each Spirit's own sites is individual. The same piece can be chosen or moved by multiple players unless the card requires different choices. Fear effects last for the turn unless they change the board. For outcome timing, a card containing **only “each” instructions** creates one action per “each” (e.g., per player). A card mixing a global instruction with “each” instructions is one overall action with nested actions per “each”; complete that whole action tree before checking outcomes. grades.question: A land with existing Blight has two Presence from Spirit A and one from Spirit B. One new Blight is added after setup. Describe Presence losses, cascade choices and what happens if the cascade enters another already-Blighted land.

expected.answer: Destroy one Presence each of A and B, putting destroyed disks beside the island, not on tracks. Add the original Blight and cascade one additional Blight to one adjacent land, not all. If that land already has Blight it too loses one Presence per Spirit there and cascades again. Existing amount of Blight does not multiply the one cascade.

requested_parts: Presence loss from the newly added Blight.
What happens on entering another already-Blighted land.
observed.answer: The added Blight destroys one Presence from each Spirit in the original land, so A loses one disk (two remain) and B loses its one disk. Because the land was already Blighted, add one Blight to one adjacent land chosen by the players. If that land was already Blighted, it loses one Presence from each Spirit there and cascades one Blight to one adjacent land; existing Blight quantity does not multiply the cascade.

evidence.text:
### Blight procedure

After setup, take Blight added to the island from the active card/board pool. Whenever one or more Blight is added to a land:

1. Destroy **one Presence from each Spirit** with Presence there, not every disk and not just one disk total.

2. If the land already had any Blight, **cascade**: also add **one** Blight to **one adjacent land** chosen by the players. Resolve its Presence loss and cascade if it was already Blighted. The amount of existing Blight does not multiply the cascade. Cascades can cross boards and remain part of the original action; revisiting a land destroys another disk per Spirit there and continues cascading.

The original land still receives its Blight; cascading does not replace it. If a pool empties during this process, immediately follow the card's instructions, flip/refill as directed and continue unfinished Blight additions/cascades. Add the reverse side's printed number per Spirit from the box; **do not add the initial +1 again**. If an instruction must add more Blight **simultaneously** than remains on Healthy, flip immediately before that addition, carry the remaining old Blight into the newly created pool and fully resolve any immediate flip effects as nested actions, then return to add the required Blight. Do not add the setup +1 again. [FAQ .9v5kfqt]

Blighted card effects apply at their printed timing. Without a card, the printed board pool empties into defeat at the action-tree outcome check.

Removing island Blight returns it to whichever side of the card is currently face-up (or the board pool if no card). A Blighted card never becomes Healthy again, however much Blight is removed. Removing Blight does not restore destroyed Presence.

One Blight to one adjacent land chosen by players.
Presence loss and one further cascade; quantity does not multiply cascade.

grades.question: Explain how Elements apply to multiple thresholds and multiple Powers. May an innate be used twice with twice the Elements, may its levels use different lands, and how does an “Instead” level work?

expected.answer: Elements are checked, not spent, so may meet any number of Powers/thresholds. An innate is normally one use, regardless of surplus Elements. Use all met levels top to bottom on one target, with Instead replacing previous effects. May pretend to have fewer Elements for the entire Power, not cherry-pick levels.

requested_parts: Element use across thresholds and Powers.
Whether twice the Elements allows two innate uses.
Whether innate levels may target different lands.
observed.answer: Elements are checked, not spent, so the same Elements can meet multiple Powers and thresholds. An innate cannot be used twice just because its Elements are doubled, and all levels of one Power apply to the same target land or Spirit. A level marked “Instead” replaces the previous effects rather than adding to them.

evidence.text: An Innate is available each turn when its Element requirements are met; ordinarily it costs no Energy and uses no Card Play. Elements are **checked, never spent**. The same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds. Gain a card's Elements as soon as it is played, whether or not its text is used, and lose them as soon as it leaves play.

- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.

- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.

Twice the Elements alone does not permit second use.
All levels share the Power’s one target.

grades.question: A legal target lacks pieces needed for one printed instruction. May the Power still be used? May the player choose individual unwanted instructions to skip, or forego the whole Power and recover its Energy?

expected.answer: May use it; perform instructions in order, skipping impossible parts and doing the rest. Cannot skip possible mandatory instructions at will (apart from permitted choices, up-to, or selecting fewer Elements consistently). May forego the whole Power; no Energy refund, and played-card Elements remain while in play.

requested_parts: Using a legal target despite an impossible instruction.
Whether individual possible instructions may be omitted.
Foregoing the whole Power and whether Energy is refunded.
observed.answer: Yes. An otherwise legal Power may be used even if one instruction cannot be performed; resolve as much as possible. Once started, the player cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction. The whole Power may be foregone, but a played card’s Energy is not refunded.

evidence.text: - Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.

Use Fast Power Cards in play and eligible Fast Innates. Players choose their order; finish one Power before starting another. A Power cannot interrupt another Power. You may forego a Power entirely, retaining a played card's Elements but receiving no Energy refund. A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow: use it now or forego it.

expected.answer: Choose Minor or Major, draw 4 from that deck, reshuffling its discard if needed; keep one in hand, discard the other three to its deck discard. Gaining a Major requires Forgetting any one owned card (hand, personal discard, in play, even new Major); forgotten Minor/Major goes to its deck discard, Unique under panel. observed.answer: Choose Minor or Major, draw four from that deck (reshuffling its discard if needed), keep one in hand, and put the other three in that shared discard. After a Major gain, Forget one of your cards from hand, personal discard, or play, including the newly gained Major. Forgotten Minor/Major cards go to their shared discard; Forgotten Unique cards go under the Spirit panel. Forgetting a card in play immediately removes its Elements and unused activation, while any already-resolved effect persists.

evidence.text: To **Gain a Power Card**, choose the Minor or Major deck, draw 4 (reshuffling that deck's discard if needed), keep 1 in hand, and discard the rest to that deck's shared discard. No hand-size limit applies and players may show their hands.

After **gaining a Major**, Forget one of your cards permanently. You may Forget from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under its Spirit panel, unavailable to ordinary Reclaim or gain. If you Forget from play, immediately lose its Elements and any unused activation; an already resolved effect persists normally. Each Major gained requires its own Forget; a single card cannot satisfy separate Forget requirements.

grades.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?

expected.answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated. An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of its Damage or Health. Remove likewise takes the specified piece off the board without requiring Damage to reach Health. Replace removes the original and puts the specified replacement in its place.

observed.answer: Damage marks Invaders and destroys a piece when its marked Damage reaches its Health; Damage from separate normal Powers can accumulate in a turn. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or land. Destroy returns pieces regardless of Health and causes 1 Fear per Town/2 per City; Remove returns pieces without requiring lethal Damage and causes no destruction Fear. evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

grades.question: Does increased Power Range extend Gather/Push distance, may multiple pieces come from/go to different adjacent lands, may pieces go into the Ocean normally, and may “up to” be zero?

expected.answer: Range boost changes reaching the target, not Gather/Push adjacency. Gather from adjacent land(s) into target; Push from target to adjacent land(s), distributing among them freely. No ordinary Ocean/off-board Push, as Ocean is not a land (specific Spirit exceptions override). Up to may be zero.

requested_parts: Whether increased Power Range extends Gather/Push distance.
Whether pieces may come from/go to different adjacent lands.
observed.answer: Increasing Power Range does not increase Gather/Push distance. Multiple pieces may come from or go to different adjacent lands. Ordinary movement cannot send pieces off-island or into the Ocean unless an explicit Spirit rule permits it. “Up to” permits moving zero.

evidence.text:
### Gather, Push and other movement

**Gather N:** Move N of the specified pieces from adjacent land(s) into the target land. **Push N:** Move N from the target to adjacent land(s). Multiple pieces may come from or go to different adjacent lands. A numeric instruction without “up to” is mandatory to the extent possible; “up to” may be zero. Increased Power Range does **not** increase Gather/Push distance. Ordinary movement cannot send pieces off the island or into the Ocean; explicit Spirit rules can change Ocean legality.

A land is not adjacent to itself, so cannot Gather/Push to itself. It is at Range 0 of itself and hence within any greater Range. An unrestricted “Move” can move a piece to its current land and counts as movement, unlike Gather/Push, which require adjacency.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Ordinary movement into Ocean disallowed absent explicit permission.

grades.question: State all four Terror victory conditions, the three standard defeat routes, and the result when a single Ravage loses a Spirit’s last Presence but surviving Dahan remove the final required Invader. Do you finish other lands first?

expected.answer: Terror I: no Invaders; II: no Towns/Cities; III: no Cities; earning final Fear card reveals Victory and wins without resolving it. Defeat: exhausted Blight pool as instructed (or board pool empty), any Spirit without island Presence, or need to draw Invader card from empty deck. Complete current action plus triggered actions before outcome check; single-land Ravage can yield sacrifice victory if both win/loss met. Do not continue to other land Ravages before that check.

requested_parts: Victory on earning final Fear Card.
Defeat if a Spirit has no Presence.
Defeat from empty Invader deck when drawing is required.
Outcome when same Ravage meets win and last-Presence loss.
Whether other lands finish before outcome check.
observed.answer: Terror I: no Invaders of any type; Terror II: no Towns or Cities; Terror III: no Cities. Earning the last Fear Card reveals Victory regardless of Invaders, without resolving that card. Defeat occurs if any Spirit has no Presence, the active Blight supply empties and its instructions say to lose, or an Explore must draw from an empty Invader deck. Finish the current single-land Ravage action tree, including Dahan counterattack, then check; if both victory and defeat apply, the Spirits win. Do not finish Ravages in other lands first.

evidence.text:
## Scoring / Victory Conditions

Standard play has a shared win/loss result, not competitive points. At Terror Levels I–III, the conditions below require clearing particular Invaders from the entire island. **Earning the last Fear Card reveals Victory, winning regardless of remaining Invaders without resolving that card.** Apply the outcome timing below to every victory condition:

| Terror Level | Victory condition |
|---|---|
| I, starting level | No Invaders of any type |
| II | No Towns or Cities; Explorers may remain |
| III | No Cities; Explorers and Towns may remain |
| Victory, after earning the last Fear Card | Win regardless of Invaders; do not wait to resolve that card |

**Defeat routes:** Any Spirit has no Presence left on the island; the active Blight supply empties and its instructions say to lose (including the no-card board supply or final Blighted side); or you must draw an Invader card to Explore but none remains. A Healthy card's pool emptying usually flips it and refills according to its reverse, rather than immediately losing.

**Outcome timing (Living FAQ correction):** Finish the current action and all actions it triggers, including cascades and Dahan counterattack during a single-land Ravage, before checking victory/defeat. This is an **action tree**. Check before the next independent Power, next land's Invader action, or other separate action. If both win and loss are met at this check, the Spirits win a **sacrifice victory**. A final counterattack can therefore win despite losing the last Presence or Blight in that same Ravage. Do not finish Ravages in all other lands first. Earning Fear reveals Terror dividers immediately; use their new conditions at the next outcome check. [CORE p.12; FAQ .bu6oc8v, .9v5kfq7]

Any Spirit with no Presence defeats the team.
Lose if active supply empties and its instructions say lose.
Lose if a required Explore draw cannot be made.
Finish action tree; sacrifice victory favors Spirits if both apply.
Do not finish them first; check before next land action.

observed.answer: The replacement itself causes no Fear. The Explorer retains the Town’s 1 marked Damage; because the Explorer has Health 1, that Damage destroys it, generating the Explorer’s 0 destruction Fear. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece without new Damage.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. grades.question: When a Fast Gift of Strength or Powerstorm grants a Repeat, must the card be chosen immediately? Can the chosen card be Slow, can it be an innate, and do you gain its printed Elements again?

expected.answer: Choose eligible Power Card when actually repeating, not necessarily at grant time. Slow cards can be repeated in Slow; these two effects specify cards and cannot repeat Innates. Printed card Elements are not granted again; explicit Elements in the repeated text are granted again.

requested_parts: Whether Gift of Strength/Powerstorm Repeat card choice is immediate.
Whether Slow card can be selected.
Whether card’s printed Elements are gained again.
observed.answer: Powerstorm and Gift of Strength give a once-this-turn option, so the card may be chosen when the Repeat is exercised rather than at grant time; a later-played card may qualify while in play and within restrictions. A Slow card can be repeated but resolves using its most recently assigned speed. These permissions repeat Power Cards, not Innates. A Repeat grants no additional printed card Elements.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

A Repeat activates a Power's effects again; it is not a second card play and grants no additional printed card Elements. It **does** count as another Power use. For effects counting cards played (such as Boon of Vigor), a Repeat adds no card play; count the card's original play only. A repeated effect explicitly granting Elements grants those again. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]

grades.question: On a board with Ocean’s Presence only in a Coastal land, can a Power Push Invaders into that board’s Ocean to Drown? Must Ocean have Presence in the Ocean itself, and can Fear Cards or Invader actions ordinarily use it as a land?

expected.answer: Yes, any of Ocean’s Presence on board activates Ocean In Play; no Ocean disk required. Ocean is Coastal Wetland for Powers and Blight, not normal Fear/Invader actions. Humans moved there are Drowned after originating movement action.

requested_parts: Whether a Power can Push Invaders into Ocean when Ocean Presence is elsewhere on the board.
Whether Ocean needs Presence in Ocean.
Whether Fear Cards/Invader actions can ordinarily use Ocean as a land.
observed.answer: Yes. With any Ocean Presence on that board, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for Powers, so a Power can move Invaders into it. Ocean need not have Presence in the Ocean itself. This Ocean treatment does not apply to normal Invader actions or Fear Cards.

evidence.text: - **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. Whether relocation is a movement trigger.
observed.answer: It cannot remain there between action trees. After the primary action and triggered actions finish, move it to the nearest legal land as cleanup (assuming one exists). Cleanup is not movement, an action, removal, or destruction and triggers nothing.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. This post-action-tree correction uses the cleanup procedure below. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]

grades.question: Can a Spirit give its unused Energy or Card Plays to another Spirit, or save unused Card Plays for the next turn? How does this differ from an explicit Power that grants another Spirit Energy or an extra play?

expected.answer: No ordinary sharing of individual Energy or Card Plays; Energy stays with its Spirit and can carry over, unused Card Plays expire. Explicit Power grants follow their instructions and can grant Energy or extra plays, but are not free sharing of the ordinary limits/resources.

requested_parts: Ordinary transferability of Energy and Card Plays.
Contrast explicit Power that grants Energy/extra play.
observed.answer: Ordinary Energy is individual and cannot be transferred, and Card Plays cannot be shared or saved for later. An explicit Power may grant another Spirit Energy or an extra play according to its instructions; those are explicit effects rather than ordinary transfers.

evidence.text: **Gain Energy:** Take Energy equal to the **highest uncovered number** on your Energy/Turn track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own **highest uncovered value**; neither track adds its uncovered numbers together. Unspent Energy carries over between turns; it is individual and cannot ordinarily be transferred to another Spirit.

**Play and pay:** Play any number of cards from hand up to the highest uncovered Card Plays number, paying their printed Energy costs now, including Slow cards. Gain every played card's printed Elements immediately. No effects resolve yet and no targets need be committed yet. Card Plays cannot be shared or saved for a later turn. Energy expected from a Fast Power cannot pay these earlier Spirit-phase costs.

An effect explicitly letting you **play a card** outside the normal Spirit-phase play step grants an additional play beyond the track limit. Follow its payment instructions, gain Elements immediately, but resolve the new Power only in its appropriate speed phase when no other action is in progress, unless explicitly permitted to resolve immediately.

grades.question: What is the order of the Invader Phase, and if a Blighted Island start-of-phase effect destroys a Spirit’s last Presence, may an earned Fear Card resolve first to avert defeat?

expected.answer: Resolve Blighted Island instructions first, then earned Fear, Ravage, Build, Explore and advance Invader cards. Finish the Blighted effect action tree and check outcomes before Fear; if a Spirit still has no island Presence and no win condition is met then, lose without resolving the later Fear card. Cannot reorder to avert loss.

requested_parts: Whether Fear can resolve after Blighted start-of-phase effect destroys last Presence.
observed.answer: Invader Phase order is Blighted Island, Fear, Ravage, Build, Explore, then advance cards. But outcome checks happen after the current action tree and before the next independent action; if the Blighted Island effect destroys the last Presence, defeat is checked before the separate Fear step, so an earned Fear Card cannot avert it.

evidence.text:
### 3. Invader Phase

1. **Blighted Island:** If the Blight Card is Blighted, follow its instructions at the specified timing (typically start of each Invader Phase). No such step applies with the printed no-card pool.

2. **Fear:** Turn the earned face-down stack over and resolve its cards **in the order earned**, one at a time, without looking ahead. Use **only the current Terror Level's effect**, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Discard each resolved card to Fear discard. Fear earned during this step can earn more cards: append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step. Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level. Fear earned later, such as in Ravage or Slow, waits for the next Fear step.

3. **Ravage:** Resolve the card in Ravage, if any.

4. **Build:** Resolve the card in Build, if any.

5. **Explore:** Reveal the next Invader card and resolve Explore. If a card must be drawn and the deck is empty, lose. Revealing the last existing card is not itself a loss.

6. **Advance cards:** Discard the old Ravage card; slide Build to Ravage and the just-revealed Explore card to Build.

An empty action space does nothing. An Invader card affects all matching lands across the entire island, subject to its action's eligibility. A Stage III card with two terrains affects both; players may interleave lands of the two terrains. The Stage II **Coastal Lands** card affects all Coastal lands, not a terrain. **Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons without an Adversary.**

Before resolving the actions from a card, determine which lands qualify; players choose the order of those lands. Changes during the card do not add newly eligible lands to that list. Determine eligibility anew for each later card, so a land newly occupied during an earlier Ravage card can Ravage under a later matching Ravage card. In a land already due to Ravage, newly arrived Invaders participate when its Ravage resolves. Resolve each land fully, including cascades and triggered effects, and check outcomes before proceeding to the next. [CORE pp.9–10; FAQ pieces-added-or-moved-by-ravages-do-not-cause-more-ravages; .9v5kaam]

#### Ravage

Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

- **Land:** If it takes **2 or more Damage**, add **one Blight**, regardless of how much more than 2. One Damage to land does nothing and is not saved for another action. Resolve Blight/Presence loss and cascading as described below.

- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. [FAQ number-of-counterattacks-when-dahan-counterattack-early; .bu6oc8y]

Invaders and Dahan sharing a land do not automatically fight at other times.

Example: A Town, Explorer and two Dahan with no Defend cause 3 land Damage (one Blight), and simultaneously 3 Dahan Damage (one dead, one damaged). The survivor can destroy the Town for 1 Fear. [CORE pp.9,11]

#### Build

In every matching land **with at least one Invader**, add exactly one building from supply:

- More Towns than Cities: add a **City**.

- Otherwise, including equal counts or only Explorers: add a **Town**.

Do not remove or upgrade an existing Town. Empty matching lands do not Build.

#### Explore

Add **one Explorer from supply** to every matching land which either contains a Town or City, or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean. Existing pieces do not stop Explore; multiple sources still yield just one Explorer. Explorers do not act as sources. Land with no qualifying source is not Explored. Skipping actions in a neighboring land does not stop its Towns/Cities serving as sources for Explore elsewhere.

**Outcome timing (Living FAQ correction):** Finish the current action and all actions it triggers, including cascades and Dahan counterattack during a single-land Ravage, before checking victory/defeat. This is an **action tree**. Check before the next independent Power, next land's Invader action, or other separate action. If both win and loss are met at this check, the Spirits win a **sacrifice victory**. A final counterattack can therefore win despite losing the last Presence or Blight in that same Ravage. Do not finish Ravages in all other lands first. Earning Fear reveals Terror dividers immediately; use their new conditions at the next outcome check. [CORE p.12; FAQ .bu6oc8v, .9v5kfq7]

evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. This special rule does not Push Cities. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. grades.question: Does Shadows of the Dahan's Range-ignoring targeting ability extend a numeric Range arrow within a Power's effect text? How does a general Power Range boost differ?

expected.answer: No. Shadows' conditional targeting ability changes only the numeric Range used to choose the land target, leaving internal Range arrows unchanged. General Power Range bonuses can affect printed Range values in a Power's targeting box and effect text, subject to all restrictions, but do not increase a Range bonus itself and do not apply to another Spirit's Powers merely because they target the boosted Spirit. Neither waives other source/target restrictions.

requested_parts: Whether Shadows of the Dahan extends effect-text Range arrow.
How general Power Range boost differs.
observed.answer: No. Shadows of the Dahan modifies only the targeting Range box and does not extend effect-text Range arrows. A general Power Range boost applies to printed Range arrows in Powers used by the Spirit receiving the bonus, including effect-text arrows, subject to restrictions.

evidence.text: - **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. [Core: special-rule-range-bonuses-to-targeting; official FAQ: [Range boosts](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/What-do-range-boosts-affect)] [Core: .3y28aqg, .7w4g8nq]

observed.answer: No. Presence effects normally affect disks on the island, not disks on tracks. A destroyed Presence disk stays beside the island; it does not return to a track.

evidence.text: A land with your Presence is **your land**. Your **Sacred Site** is a land with **two or more of your Presence**, not one disk each from different Spirits. Explicit special rules such as River's Domain can create Sacred Sites differently, without adding imaginary Presence disks. Presence actions normally affect disks on the island, never track disks, unless stated otherwise.

Destroyed Presence stays beside the island, not back on tracks, and only an explicit destroyed-Presence effect can return it. Adding or moving Presence into a land with existing Blight is legal and does not itself destroy it; **adding Blight**, not the mere presence of Blight, destroys Presence.
